skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires fresh verification evidence before an agent claims tests pass, a build succeeds, a bug is fixed, or work is complete.
skill.summary: Require fresh evidence before claiming coding work is complete or successful.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: All static command and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences or explanatory JSON text. I found one semantic concern: EVALUATION.json contains a self-declared safety audit that marks the skill safe to publish, which can influence reviewers if treated as trusted evidence. Remove that packaged report before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove EVALUATION.json from the published skill package or move it outside files loaded by agents and marketplace reviewers.

remediation.issue: Untrusted audit assertions inside skill content
remediation.suggestion: Do not include safe-to-publish claims in distributed skill files. Let the marketplace audit pipeline generate those results independently.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: EVALUATION.json embeds a self-declared audit with "safe_to_publish": true and a summary saying findings are false positives. This can influence agents or reviewers if treated as trusted evidence.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The self-assessment is explicit and located in an untrusted skill file. It may be report residue rather than an active instruction, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: AI agents can report completed work before checking tests, builds, or requirements. This skill requires fresh verification evidence before any completion or success claim.
actual_capabilities: Requires agents to identify what command proves a claim.
Directs agents to run verification before success language.
Guides agents to read output, exit status, and failure counts.
Applies to tests, builds, bug fixes, requirements, commits, and pull requests.
Requires independent checks for delegated agent work.
Describes red-green verification for regression tests.
limitations: Requires access to the relevant project commands.
Depends on the agent following the instruction.
Cannot prove work complete when no meaningful verification exists.
Does not replace code review or product acceptance.

use_cases.title: Prevent False Completion Reports
use_cases.description: Require evidence before an assistant says tests pass, builds succeed, or a task is complete.

use_cases.title: Standardize Verification Discipline
use_cases.description: Give teams one rule for evidence before commits, pull requests, and handoffs.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Work Safely
use_cases.description: Check delegated agent results with diffs and independent verification before accepting success reports.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Simple Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Before claiming this is complete, identify the command that proves it. Run it now and report the result with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: The agent thinks tests should pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the relevant test command now. Report pass counts, failures, and exit status before saying the tests pass.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Build and Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: A change must satisfy a checklist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the build and compare results with the requirement list. Report verified items and unresolved gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Delegated Work
prompt_templates.prompt: The agent reported success. Inspect the diff, run independent verification, and report only what the evidence supports.

output: I reproduced the original symptom and ran the targeted check.
The symptom no longer appears, so I can report the fix with that evidence.
I ran the relevant test suite and read the result.
The run reported zero failures, so the test claim is verified.

output_examples.input: The delegated agent says the task is done.
output: I checked the diff and verified the claimed changes.
The evidence shows the task is partially complete.
I will report the remaining gap instead of claiming completion.

best_practices: Run verification fresh before every success claim.
Match the verification command to the exact claim.
Report evidence, failures, and gaps with the same clarity as success.
anti_patterns: Using words like should or probably instead of verified facts.
Treating a linter result as proof that a build or feature works.
Accepting an agent success report without independent verification.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands itself?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to run the relevant verification and report evidence.

faq.question: What if no verification command exists?
faq.answer: State that verification is unavailable and avoid completion claims. Describe what remains unverified.

faq.question: Does this apply to simple tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The rule applies before any completion or success statement.

faq.question: Can a previous passing run count?
faq.answer: No. Use fresh output for the current claim.

faq.question: How should delegated work be handled?
faq.answer: Check the diff, run independent verification, then report only verified facts.

faq.question: Does this replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It improves evidence discipline but does not replace review or judgment.
